stem:
Yogesh invests $\mathrm{Rs}\,5000$ at $10\%$ per year, compounded annually, for $2$ years.

Which claim correctly gives the amount after $2$ years?

options.text: Each year adds $\mathrm{Rs}\,500$ on the original $\mathrm{Rs}\,5000$ only, so the amount is $\mathrm{Rs}\,6000$.
Compounding also covers interest paid out each year with the principal kept fixed at $\mathrm{Rs}\,5000$.
After year $1$ the amount is $\mathrm{Rs}\,5500$; year $2$ interest on $\mathrm{Rs}\,5500$ gives amount $\mathrm{Rs}\,6050$.
The amount is $10\%$, the printed rate.

teacher.key_rationale: With compounding, year 2 uses the updated amount: 5000→5500→6050. Keeping the original principal each year, treating paid-out interest as compounding, or reading the rate as the amount each miss the updated base.
